Automation Opportunity: - Cost-per-transaction auto-computed from cost ÷ volume; benchmark-delta auto-flagged
Controls: - CTL-447 (ensure controlled execution — Shared Services Performance & Analytics (PA-72.3).)
- operational: transaction-count integrity; operational: Finance Controller quarterly efficiency-review sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Benchmark-staleness risk**: the industry benchmark is years old and BuildRight's "above-benchmark" result is actually competitive; mitigated by the annual benchmark refresh in W2591

- **Cost-per-transaction-gaming risk**: a function reclassifies transactions to lower its cost-per-transaction (e.g., bundles two invoices as one); mitigated by the transaction-count integrity from the source system
System Touchpoints: - Cost accounting (links to VS-158 / W85, VS-72 / W2575) — the cost-per-transaction numerator
- Volume masters (links to VS-15 / W7 invoice count, VS-19 / W10 payslip count, VS-27 / W373 IT user count) — the denominator
- Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113) — the benchmark comparison and trend

steps.activity: Finance Analyst calculates cost-per-transaction for each shared service: AP cost per invoice processed (target: PHP 150–200), AR cost per invoice, payroll cost per payslip, IT cost per user, procurement cost per PO; compares against industry benchmarks

Analyst identifies efficiency improvement opportunities: automation potential (AP OCR, payroll automation), volume consolidation across entities, shared service center staffing optimization, technology upgrade ROI

Finance Controller presents efficiency analytics to COO and CFO: cost trend by shared service, benchmark comparison, improvement recommendations with projected savings; proposes annual efficiency targets

fields.Participants: Finance Controller, CFO, External Benchmarking Firm

Automation Opportunity: - Benchmark-dataset auto-merged with internal metrics with definition-mapping; gap-analysis auto-quantified
Controls: - CTL-447 (ensure controlled execution — Shared Services Performance & Analytics (PA-72.3).)
- Operational: CFO + COO sign-off on the benchmarking findings and targets; CEO sign-off on major transformation investment
Pain Points / Risks: - **Apples-to-oranges risk**: the benchmark defines "IT cost" differently than BuildRight, making the comparison misleading; mitigated by the definition-mapping before the benchmark and the footnoted comparison

- **Benchmark-driven-overcut risk**: a below-benchmark result triggers cost-cutting that's actually underinvestment (the function is lean but fragile); mitigated by the below-benchmark-as-underinvestment-risk lens in step 2
System Touchpoints: - Benchmarking dataset (links to VS-27 / W113, VS-72 / W2590 efficiency) — the external benchmark merged with internal metrics
- Transformation portfolio (links to VS-112 / PMO, VS-133 OpEx continuous improvement) — the approved initiatives
- Investment budget (links to VS-40 / W21 capex, VS-135 TBM/FinOps) — the transformation funding
Time Estimate: ~7 weeks/year Finance Controller + external firm = **~250–300 hours/year** Finance Controller.

steps.activity: Finance Controller engages benchmarking firm: compares BuildRight shared services cost and efficiency against Philippine retail sector peers, ASEAN retail benchmarks, global best practices; covers IT, HR, Finance, Procurement, Facilities functions

Controller analyzes benchmarking results: identifies above-benchmark costs (opportunity for reduction), below-benchmark costs (potential underinvestment risk), best practice adoption gaps; produces gap analysis with quantified improvement potential

CFO and COO review benchmarking findings: set 3-year improvement targets, approve transformation initiatives (shared service automation, process re-engineering), allocate investment budget; Finance Controller tracks progress quarterly

workflows.name: IC Profit Elimination & Consolidation Impact Analysis

Automation Opportunity: - Elimination auto-computed from the IC transactions; margin-creep auto-flagged from the trend
Controls: - CTL-447 (ensure controlled execution — Shared Services Performance & Analytics (PA-72.3).)
- CTL-447 (consolidation accuracy — links to VS-17 / W9A, W234); CTL-18 (TP arm's-length — links to W235); operational: Finance Controller elimination sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin-creep risk**: IC pricing drifts above arm's-length over time (cumulative small increases), inflating entity profit and creating a TP exposure; mitigated by the margin-trend monitoring in step 2
- **Incomplete-elimination risk**: an IC balance isn't eliminated in consolidation, distorting the consolidated financials; mitigated by the no-material-residual check in step 3
System Touchpoints: - Consolidation (links to VS-17 / W9A month-end close, W234 consolidated profit elimination) — the elimination engine
- IC pricing (links to VS-72 / W2582 agreements) — the margin source for the elimination
- TP documentation (links to VS-72 / W2594) — the margin-creep flag feeding the TP review

steps.activity: Consolidation Accountant calculates IC profit elimination: identifies IC transactions with unrealized profit (inventory transfers between entities at above-cost, IC service margins), calculates elimination amounts, posts consolidation adjustment entries

Accountant analyzes IC profit elimination trend: tracks IC margin levels by service type, identifies margin creep (IC pricing gradually increasing above arm's-length), flags high-margin IC transactions for transfer pricing review

Finance Controller reviews elimination impact on consolidated financials: ensures eliminations are complete and accurate, verifies no material IC balances remain uneliminated, confirms consolidated tax positions reflect proper elimination

workflows.name: Shared Services Staff Productivity & Capacity Planning

Automation Opportunity: - Productivity dashboard auto-refreshed quarterly; staffing-scenario auto-modeled
Controls: - CTL-447 (ensure controlled execution — Shared Services Performance & Analytics (PA-72.3).)
- CTL-447 (workforce-planning accuracy — links to VS-19); operational: COO + CFO sign-off on staffing changes
Pain Points / Risks: - **Productivity-without-context risk**: a function shows low transactions-per-FTE but handles high-complexity work (quality over quantity); mitigated by the complexity-weighting in the metric

- **Automation-vs-headcount-misjudgment risk**: an automation investment is approved when a headcount redeployment would have been cheaper; mitigated by the financial-impact modeling comparing both options in step 2
System Touchpoints: - HRIS / productivity (links to VS-19 / W34 shift scheduling, W292 employee master, VS-103 people analytics) — the FTE and productivity data
- Cost trends (links to VS-72 / W2590 efficiency) — the cost-vs-productivity correlation
- Capacity plan (links to VS-33 / strategic planning, VS-112 PMO) — the staffing and automation decisions

steps.activity: HR Business Partner compiles shared services productivity metrics: transactions per FTE per function, overtime hours, error rates, customer satisfaction scores from internal surveys; identifies capacity constraints and surplus areas

Finance Controller correlates productivity with cost trends: determines if cost increases are volume-driven (justified) or efficiency-driven (action needed); proposes staffing adjustments (hire, redeploy, automate) with financial impact modeling
COO reviews shared services capacity plan: approves staffing changes, prioritizes automation investments, sets productivity improvement targets; incorporates into annual operating plan

steps.activity: Finance Controller compiles transfer pricing documentation: intercompany transaction analysis, functional analysis (FAR — functions, assets, risks), benchmarking study, allocation methodology documentation, entity-by-entity profit analysis; engages external TP advisor for annual update

External advisor reviews documentation for BIR compliance: confirms arm's-length pricing methodology, validates benchmarking approach per BIR Revenue Regulation guidelines, prepares TP report per Philippine requirements

Finance Controller files transfer pricing documentation with BIR (mandatory for related party transactions); maintains documentation for potential BIR audit; updates methodology annually based on business changes and regulatory updates

fields.Participants: IT Finance Analyst, CIO, Finance Controller

workflows.name: Shared Services Technology Investment ROI Tracking

Automation Opportunity: - ROI auto-tracked from cost-savings vs. business-case; adoption auto-measured from system-usage telemetry
Controls: - CTL-447 (ensure controlled execution — Shared Services Performance & Analytics (PA-72.3).)

- operational: capex-approval for automation investment; CTL-637 (technology value realization — realized savings finance-validated and allocation rate adjusted); operational: CIO + Finance Controller quarterly ROI sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Savings-non-realization risk**: the automation delivers but the savings are absorbed into other cost growth (no net reduction), eroding the ROI; mitigated by the allocation-rate-adjustment in step 3 locking in the savings
- **Adoption-risk**: the automation is delivered but not adopted (staff keep the manual process); mitigated by the adoption-metric tracking in step 1 and the change-management intervention
System Touchpoints: - Automation portfolio (links to VS-30 / W398 emerging-tech PoC, VS-133 OpEx, VS-112 PMO) — the automation projects
- Cost savings (links to VS-72 / W2590 efficiency, VS-158 / W85) — the realized savings
- Allocation rates (links to VS-72 / W2574) — the rate adjustment for realized savings
Time Estimate: ~3 days/quarter IT Finance Analyst + Controller = **~180–220 hours/year**.

steps.activity: IT Finance Analyst tracks shared service automation project ROI: compares projected vs. actual cost savings (AP automation: 30% cost reduction target, payroll automation: 20% error reduction), measures adoption rates and usage metrics, calculates payback period vs. business case

Analyst identifies underperforming investments: projects not delivering projected savings, low adoption requiring change management intervention, scope creep increasing cost beyond business case; recommends corrective actions

Finance Controller incorporates automation savings into shared services cost budget: adjusts allocation rates downward for functions with realized savings, reallocates saved capacity to growth activities, updates 3-year cost forecast

workflows.name: Shared Services Entity Profitability Contribution Analysis

Controls: - CTL-447 (ensure controlled execution — Shared Services Performance & Analytics (PA-72.3).)
- CTL-447 (TP arm's-length — links to W235); CTL-213 (entity-profitability & chargeback accuracy); operational: CFO + CEO review of allocation equity
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cross-subsidization-distortion risk**: a mature entity (Depot Inc.) subsidizes a startup entity (Digital Commerce) via allocation, making the mature entity look less profitable and the startup look worse; mitigated by the strategic-investment-justification lens in step 3 (the subsidy is intentional, documented)

- **Allocation-equity-dispute risk**: an entity CFO argues the allocation is unfair (benefit ≠ cost share); mitigated by the periodic allocation-methodology review (W2574) and the external-advisor arm's-length confirmation
System Touchpoints: - Entity P&L (links to VS-17 / W9 financial close, VS-72 / W2575 allocation) — the per-entity profitability
- IC charges (links to VS-72 / W2583) — the allocated cost
- FP&A (links to VS-17 / W26 budget, VS-101 merchandise financial planning) — the entity-profitability model

steps.activity: FP&A Manager analyzes entity profitability after IC allocations: revenue per entity, cost of services including IC charges, operating margin per entity; compares entity standalone profit vs. allocated shared services cost impact

FP&A identifies cross-subsidization concerns: entities with disproportionate shared service cost allocation relative to benefit received, entities subsidizing others' growth, transfer pricing margins distorting entity profitability

CFO reviews entity profitability with CEO: discusses allocation equity, strategic investment justification (e.g., Digital Commerce Inc. startup losses funded by mature Depot Inc.), performance incentive implications; adjusts allocation methodology if significant inequity identified

workflows.name: Shared Services Annual Performance Report & Board Presentation

Automation Opportunity: - Annual report auto-rolled-up from the W2590 dashboard with year-over-year delta; Board-deck auto-generated from the strategic summary
Controls: - CTL-349: board & committee governance — annual report receipt minuted (links to VS-21 / VS-36); operational: Board Audit Committee receipt minuted

- **Board-overload risk**: the report is too detailed for a Board audience; mitigated by the CFO strategic-summary layer (step 2) translating detail into decisions
System Touchpoints: - Performance-report dataset (links to VS-27 / W113, VS-72 / W2590–W2596) — the year-round analytics rolled up
- Board reporting (links to VS-21 / W120 audit, VS-36 / W124 corporate secretary) — the Board Audit Committee artifact
- Transformation roadmap (links to VS-112 / PMO, VS-133 OpEx) — the investment proposals
Time Estimate: ~1.5 weeks Controller compilation + ~1 week CFO review + Board presentation = **~120–150 hours/year**.

steps.activity: Finance Controller compiles annual shared services performance report: total shared services cost (PHP ~150M/year), cost per entity, efficiency trend (3-year), automation progress, SLA compliance, transfer pricing compliance, benchmarking results, 3-year outlook
CFO reviews and approves report; highlights key findings and strategic recommendations for Board presentation; includes shared services transformation roadmap and investment requests

CFO presents to Board Audit Committee: shared services governance, IC transaction compliance, transfer pricing status, cost efficiency achievements, investment proposals; Board provides oversight feedback and approves major initiatives
